finding.claim: SafeListSanitizer keeps one PermitScrubber per instance and rewrites its tags and attributes on every sanitize call, so concurrent calls on a shared instance can scrub with another call's allowlist.
finding.source: Per-call tags:/attributes: options, or any caller that reuses one sanitizer instance across requests or threads.

trace.note: scrub reads options and decides which allowlist to use.
Overwrites the shared scrubber's tags on every call.
Scrubs the fragment with whatever allowlist the shared object holds at that moment.

finding.guards_checked: A new instance per .new avoids sharing in the single-threaded case; default allowlists are dup'd per class. Whether an app or Rails helper reuses an instance concurrently was not verified. Not confirmed as exploitable.

finding.claim: Attribute allowlist checks the local name (attr.name) while the URI-scheme check uses the namespace-prefixed name, so a prefixed attribute like foo:href matches href in the allowlist and skips the protocol check.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied HTML containing a namespace-prefixed attribute such as foo:href="javascript:...".
finding.sink: href/src URI attribute that reaches a browser as a live link (scrubbers.rb:169 skips scrub_uri_attribute).

trace.note: scrub_attribute? is called with attr.name (local name, e.g. href).
Attribute kept because local name is in the allowlist.
scrub_attribute builds attr_name with the namespace prefix, e.g. foo:href.
ATTR_VAL_IS_URI check uses foo:href, which is not listed, so no protocol scrub happens.

finding.guards_checked: HTML5 parser only namespaces xlink: and xml: attributes that browsers honor; xlink:href is covered by the URI check and by the SVG local-ref rule at scrubbers.rb:175-177. Arbitrary prefixes are not treated as href by browsers in HTML5 mode. HTML4 (libxml2) path not verified. Low confidence; hardening rather than confirmed exploit.
